formula_checks.name: extraIncome
formula_checks.reviewer_why: A supposedly one-time payment with no year recurs every year; missing timing is treated as recurring income. General taxability also needs source-specific classification.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Require a year for a one-time item; keep it pending if absent. Preserve actual payment month and source tax treatment.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: A one-time amount with no year counts in every year. Its second point is also real: every benefit is put in untaxed income, and the Benefits step says "We won't tax this income." even when Unemployment is chosen — unemployment compensation is taxed income.
formula_checks.plain_example: One-time $2,000, no year: counted every year. $1,000 a month of unemployment: $0 taxed; right $12,000 a year taxed.
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-INCOME-B): money that lands once lands in its own year and month (landsOnce): a one-time payment with no year waits — "year not entered" — in no year, no month and no tax; a signing bonus is asked its month (signingDate) and lands once. Unemployment pay is taxed (IRC §85(a), IRS Publication 525; unemploymentMonthly): $1,000 a month is $12,000 taxed, and the Benefits step says so (it said "We won't tax this income.").

formula_checks.name: tipsAnnual
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Counts months in which either earner has any salary; a tipped earner’s employment months can differ from the household’s.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Associate tips with the correct earner and paid months; retain the current result only for an explicitly household-wide monthly tip input.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: One household tips figure × the months any earner is paid. Tips cannot belong to one earner, and no screen writes the field. Records fix: the card should say it is one household figure, written by no screen today.
formula_checks.plain_example: Tips $313.17 for a spouse paid 6 months while the other is paid 12: the app reads 12 months, $3,758.04.

needs_a_ruling.item: Whether vested shares are money in the bank
needs_a_ruling.reading_a: they land as money in March, $1,000 less the rate (what the app does)
needs_a_ruling.reading_b: $1,000 is taxed income in March but not money to spend until the shares are sold; they sit in Net worth
needs_a_ruling.recommendation: Reading b, with a "sold when they vest" choice that makes them land as money. It is how his DEC-0179 treats reinvested dividends (taxed, not spendable), and tenet 7 (nothing made to look better than it is). DEC-0012 settles the month, not whether it is cash.
